questions.question: Which statement is verifiable as a fact?
choices: The library opened in 1984
The library is the best building in town
Everyone should visit the library
The library feels welcoming

questions.question: Which statement is an opinion?
choices: The schedule lists six class periods
The new schedule is more convenient than the old one
The first class begins at 8:10 a.m.
The schedule was posted online

questions.question: A news story quotes only people who support a proposal. What possible bias should a reader consider?
choices: The dates must be incorrect
The proposal cannot be discussed
Opposing perspectives may be missing
Every quotation is fictional

questions.question: Why is a statistic not automatically free from bias?
choices: Numbers can never be checked
Statistics contain no information
All statistics are opinions
Choices about collection, comparison, and presentation can shape its meaning

questions.question: Which source detail is most relevant when judging a claim about a medical treatment?
choices: The quality of evidence and the source's expertise or interests
The number of colors on the website
The length of the headline
Whether the source uses a logo

questions.question: A poll of 20 volunteers at a sports event is used to describe all residents. What is the main concern?
choices: The poll has too many respondents
The sample may not represent the full population
Volunteers cannot answer questions
Residents have no opinions

questions.question: Which sentence combines a fact with an opinion?
choices: The park has three courts
The park opened last summer
The park has three courts, making it the city's finest recreation space
The park is located beside the school

questions.question: A product page reports only positive customer reviews and omits how reviews were selected. What should a reader ask?
choices: Whether every product has a page
Whether the page has a title
Whether the reviews use complete sentences
Whether the reviews are representative and what evidence was left out

questions.question: Which phrase most clearly signals an opinion?
choices: The most effective solution
At a distance of two kilometers
On September 14
According to the posted data

questions.question: A chart begins its vertical axis at 95 rather than zero, making a small difference look large. What should readers examine?
choices: The color of the chart title
The scale and how it affects the visual comparison
Whether the chart has a caption
The alphabetical order of labels

questions.question: An author describes one group as 'concerned residents' and another as 'complainers.' What does this wording suggest?
choices: A neutral comparison of both groups
A verified count of participants
Uneven framing that may reveal bias
An explanation of the issue's timeline

questions.question: Which evidence best supports an objective claim that a bus route became faster?
choices: A rider's statement that it feels faster
A campaign slogan about efficiency
A photograph of the bus
Recorded travel times from comparable trips before and after the change

questions.question: A claim is repeated by many websites, all citing the same original post. What does this indicate?
choices: Repetition does not equal independent confirmation
The claim is proven by the number of pages
The original post is necessarily false
Each website conducted a new study

questions.question: Which question helps distinguish an opinion from a fact?
choices: Does the statement sound confident?
Can reliable evidence verify the statement as written?
Is the statement printed in a large font?
Does the author agree with me?

questions.question: A report describes a policy's costs but not its benefits. What is a fair next step?
choices: Assume the policy has no benefits
Reject every fact in the report
Seek additional sources that examine the omitted side
Repeat the report's conclusion

questions.question: An influencer recommends a product and receives payment from its seller. What should readers consider?
choices: Payment guarantees the product works
The recommendation is a scientific study
The seller cannot be identified
The financial relationship may affect how the recommendation is presented

questions.question: Which sentence is most clearly an observable fact?
choices: The container holds 500 milliliters
The container is unattractive
The container is too large
The container is the best choice

questions.question: A writer uses only examples that support a claim while ignoring stronger contrary evidence. This is
choices: a random sample
cherry-picking evidence
a neutral summary
a controlled variable

questions.question: Why should a reader separate a source's evidence from its conclusion?
choices: Evidence always proves every conclusion
Conclusions are always facts
The conclusion may extend beyond what the evidence supports
Evidence cannot be interpreted

questions.question: Two reports give different estimates because they use different date ranges. What should a reader compare?
choices: Their website colors
The authors' preferred headlines
The number of images
Their methods and the time periods measured
